title: Executor decommissioning: the lifecycle that makes scale-down safe
purpose: Executor decommission lifecycle. Scale-down decision; Stop scheduling new tasks; Migrate shuffle blocks; Update block locations; Executor exits safely; What happens without it.
accessibleSummary: Executor decommission lifecycle. Scale-down decision; Stop scheduling new tasks; Migrate shuffle blocks; Update block locations; Executor exits safely; What happens without it.
longDescription: Executor decommission lifecycle. Scale-down decision; Stop scheduling new tasks; Migrate shuffle blocks; Update block locations; Executor exits safely; What happens without it.

nodes.label: 1. Mark for decommission
nodes.summary: The executor is flagged for removal rather than terminated immediately.
nodes.detail: The executor is flagged for removal rather than terminated immediately.
nodes.whyItMatters: The executor is flagged for removal rather than terminated immediately.

evidence.note: Spark needs a mechanism to decommission an executor gracefully by preserving its state before removing it.

drill.example: Autoscale determines the pool can shrink after a burst of work completes.
failureModes: With decommissioning disabled, the executor is simply removed with its data.

nodes.label: 2. Stop scheduling new tasks
nodes.summary: No new tasks are scheduled while running work finishes.
nodes.detail: No new tasks are scheduled while running work finishes.
nodes.whyItMatters: No new tasks are scheduled while running work finishes.

evidence.note: Graceful decommissioning preserves executor state before removal rather than terminating mid-work.

outputs: An executor with no new obligations
drill.example: Two in-flight tasks finish while no further tasks are scheduled onto the node.
failureModes: A long-running task delays the whole decommission sequence.

nodes.label: 3. Migrate shuffle blocks
nodes.summary: Shuffle blocks are copied to a peer executor or to fallback storage.
nodes.detail: Shuffle blocks are copied to a peer executor or to fallback storage.
nodes.whyItMatters: Shuffle blocks are copied to a peer executor or to fallback storage.

evidence.note: Shuffle blocks are migrated to a peer executor, or to configured fallback storage if no peer has room.
Shuffle migration is one of the four cooperating parts of Efficient Scaledown.

inputs: A peer with capacity or fallback storage
processing: Copy blocks to their new home
drill.example: Blocks move to a peer executor over the network before the source node exits.
failureModes: No peer capacity and no fallback storage configured leaves blocks with nowhere to go.

nodes.label: 4. Update block locations
nodes.summary: Block location metadata is re-pointed to the blocks' new home.
nodes.detail: Block location metadata is re-pointed to the blocks' new home.
nodes.whyItMatters: Block location metadata is re-pointed to the blocks' new home.

evidence.note: Shuffle state must remain resolvable for reduce tasks after the producing executor is gone.

outputs: Reduce tasks resolve to the new location
drill.example: A reducer scheduled later fetches from the peer rather than the departed executor.
failureModes: Stale location metadata sends a fetch to a node that no longer exists.

nodes.label: 5. Executor exits safely
nodes.summary: The executor terminates only once every block has a new home.
nodes.detail: The executor terminates only once every block has a new home.
nodes.whyItMatters: The executor terminates only once every block has a new home.

evidence.note: The executor exits only once its state has been preserved elsewhere.

outputs: Reclaimed compute with no outstanding obligation
drill.example: The pool shrinks by one node and billing for it stops, with no downstream failure.
failureModes: Terminating before confirmation reintroduces exactly the failure decommissioning prevents.

nodes.label: Without decommissioning
nodes.summary: Skipping decommissioning loses the blocks and forces a full stage recompute.
nodes.detail: Skipping decommissioning loses the blocks and forces a full stage recompute.
nodes.whyItMatters: Skipping decommissioning loses the blocks and forces a full stage recompute.

evidence.note: When an executor holding shuffle data is lost, Spark raises FetchFailedException and must re-execute the affected stage.
Removing an executor before a shuffle completes means its shuffle files must be recomputed unnecessarily.

drill.example: A ten-minute map stage runs twice because one node was reclaimed early.
controls: Enable decommissioning or remote shuffle storage
failureModes: Repeated losses produce a retry storm where progress stalls entirely.

edges.label: Flagged executor stops taking new work
Draining allows block migration to begin
Terminating without migration loses the blocks
Recompute regenerates what was not migrated
